title: Return a flat model principal quotient to an affine chart of the original scheme
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with affine opens $U_1=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, $f(U_1)\subseteq V$, and $B$ finitely presented over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $A_0\to A$ be a ring map, $B_0$ a commutative $A_0$-algebra, and $e:A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ an $A$-algebra isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $x\in U_1$ correspond to $\mathfrak q\subset B$, let $a_0,g_0\in B_0$, and put $a=e(1\otimes a_0)$ and $g=e(1\otimes g_0)$. Assume $a\in\mathfrak q$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, and $H_0=(B_0)_{g_0}/(a_0)$ is flat over $A_0$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Then $U=D(g)=\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ is an affine open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$, the restriction $a|_U$ has the same germ at $x$ as $a$, and $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B_g/(a))\hookrightarrow U$ is a closed immersion containing $x$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_{A_0}H_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g/(a)$ given by $c\otimes\overline{b_0/g_0^n}\mapsto\overline{c\,e(1\otimes b_0)/g^n}$. The quotient $B_g/(a)$ is flat and finitely presented over $A$, and the actual composite $D\to U\to X\to S$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

proof.text: By the affine basic-open lemmas, g outside the prime of x puts x in the affine open D(g). The presheaf germ_res_apply identity gives equality of the restricted and original germs. Let j be Spec(B_g) → Spec(B) → X. The range of Spec(B_g) → Spec(B) is D(g), so the image formula for the affine chart gives range(j)=D_X(g). The open-immersion isomorphism with the inclusion of D_X(g) gives i with i.hom followed by inclusion equal to j. Lift the prime of x along the localization spectrum map. Its lifted prime contains a/1 because its contraction contains a. The quotient-spectrum image is precisely the primes containing (a/1), so it supplies a quotient point mapping to x. The quotient map is a closed immersion, and composition with i.hom preserves this property.

proof.text: Put C₀=(B₀)_{g₀}. Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.tensorProductEquivTMulRight identifies A ⊗ C₀ with the localization of A ⊗ B₀ away from 1 ⊗ g₀. Transport the localization through e using IsLocalization.algEquivOfAlgEquiv and e(1 ⊗ g₀)=g. Their composite L is an A-algebra isomorphism to B_g. Its formula on c ⊗ (b₀/1) follows from the two generator formulas and e being A-linear. Since L preserves multiplication and sends 1 ⊗ (g₀/1) to g/1, uniqueness of a multiplicative inverse shows that it sends 1 ⊗ invSelf(g₀) to invSelf(g). Multiplication and powers then give the required fraction formula.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, second proof paragraph: return from the cartesian model. Expanded using the algebra and scheme tags specified in the steps.

proof.text: Let I₀ be the ideal generated by a₀/1 in C₀. Apply Algebra.TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv to identify A ⊗ (C₀/I₀) with (A ⊗ C₀)/(1 ⊗ I₀). The generator formula for L and ha show that L carries this extended principal ideal to (a/1). Ideal.quotientEquivAlg therefore transports this quotient to B_g/(a/1). This constructs E. On c ⊗ class(b₀/g₀^n), the tensor quotient formula, the quotient equivalence formula, and the fraction formula for L give exactly the claimed value. Flatness of A ⊗ H₀ over A is Module.Flat.baseChange, and E.symm.toLinearEquiv transfers it to H.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, second proof paragraph: return from the cartesian model. Expanded using the algebra and scheme tags specified in the steps.

proof.text: Use Mathlib IsLocalization.Away.finitePresentation, which proves finite presentation of B_g over B by the one-generator localization presentation B[z]/(gz-1). Transitivity with the given finite presentation of B over A makes B_g finitely presented over A. The ideal generated by a/1 is finitely generated by Submodule.fg_span_singleton. Algebra.FinitePresentation.quotient then gives the required finite presentation of H=B_g/(a/1) over A.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, second proof paragraph: return from the cartesian model. Expanded using the algebra and scheme tags specified in the steps.

proof.text: The factorization i.hom followed by the basic-open inclusion equals Spec(B → B_g) followed by the original affine chart. The affine induced-ring-map square and hcompat identify the actual composite Spec(H) → X → S with Spec(A → H) followed by hV.fromSpec. The scalar-tower algebra-map identities verify that this is the canonical A-algebra structure on H. Apply Flat.SpecMap_iff and LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff to the established flatness and finite presentation of H over A. Finally compose each morphism property with the open immersion hV.fromSpec. This proves both properties of the actual composite, without assumptions on f outside the selected charts.
